task: Add TS/Lattice foundation for a headless authority-enforce runner: typed runner contracts, canonical Ed25519 signing helpers, and AuthorityClient methods for Python authority runner endpoints.
outcome: Developers can run authority runner contract/client smoke tests and see deterministic signing plus expected endpoint calls pass, while ordinary local/shadow evidence is still not promoted to receipt-backed L2+.
facts: Python authority already exposes policy, actor key, runner register/heartbeat, job claim/lease, provider-events, evidence and receipt concepts.
Current TS/Lattice has authority_status, authority_enforce_policy, verification evidence POST paths, and authority-boundary classification, but no headless runner loop or signing primitives.
Mac Runner V4 has a stronger live runner behavior model; this story only adds TS contract/client foundations, not production execution orchestration.
Existing authority_status must continue to report productionDone false and receiptVerified false unless a verified server receipt is available.
constraints: Use existing authority-client and authority-boundary patterns; do not invent a second truth source.
Do not make local/off workflows require Python authority server or paid infrastructure.
Do not claim L2+ from unsigned local JSON, shadow POST attempts, or status output.
Keep implementation bounded to TS contracts, signing helpers, client methods, and smoke tests for milestones 1-2.
unknowns: Exact Python receipt response shape may vary; client parsing should preserve unknown fields without overclaiming verification.
The later runner loop will decide CLI provider command execution and secure key storage details.
